rules.name: Sold out
rules.why: No size or colour can be bought, so a customer would be sent to a dead end.

rules.name: No image
rules.why: Every card needs a real nicobar.com image, and there is none to show.

rules.name: No description
rules.why: After cleaning there is no site copy left, so the writer would have to invent one.

rules.name: Hidden on the site
rules.why: Nicobar has hidden it from shoppers, and a link would show them what the site does not.

rules.name: Gift card
rules.why: A gift card is not a product to write about. These are removed before the snapshot, so they have no row.

rules.name: Reasons not recorded
rules.why: This snapshot was built before every reason was kept. Rebuild it: until then nothing excluded can be overridden.

rules.name: Bundle
rules.why: A shop-bundle row is several products sold as one, not one product to write about.
rules.if_enabled: Ranks as one product. The writer sees its title and description only, not its parts.

rules.name: Out of season
rules.why: Its subcategory is listed in config/season.json for a festival that is not now. Rakhi only, today.
rules.if_enabled: Ranks normally. A draft that names the festival still fails the season check for that customer alone.

rules.name: Thin description
rules.why: Fewer than 20 words of site copy, so the writer has little to ground a claim on.
rules.if_enabled: The word count is a check on the build only, so a run takes the product. The writer has under 20 words to ground on: a claim beyond them fails check C7, and that customer's draft fails alone.

rules.name: No class tag
rules.why: One-per-kind rows and class sections read this tag. Without it the product can pass only as a plain pick.
rules.if_enabled: Ranks as a plain pick, never in a class section or a fitted trip pool, and only one such product per row.

rules.name: No category tag
rules.why: Rows read the category for gender and home. Without it the product reads as neutral wear.
rules.if_enabled: Reads as wear, never as home, and as no gender unless its gender tag says so.

rules.name: Alphabet pieces
rules.why: A ranking bar. An alphabet piece implies an initial, and we do not choose one for a customer.
rules.if_enabled: Ranks like any other product. Nothing checks the initial against the customer.

rules.name: Gift sets
rules.why: A ranking bar, kept out of every generated row since the wide run. No further reason is on record.

rules.name: Pet accessories
rules.why: A ranking bar, kept out of every generated row since the wide run. No further reason is on record.
